paragraphs: Excavations at a Bronze Age hilltop settlement in the north of a river valley have uncovered several thousand fragments of a fine painted pottery whose style is otherwise known only from workshops some 300 kilometers to the south. Several archaeologists infer that the settlement carried on regular trade with those southern workshops. Others contend that the pottery was made on site by immigrant potters trained in the southern tradition, pointing to a kiln at the settlement built to a southern design. The kiln, however, has yielded only fragments of coarse cooking ware, and no tools for painting have been recovered anywhere on the site.
